title: R29 LLM filter prompt: enforce economic plausibility question format with explicit output schema
rationale: R29 is queued as 'LLM semantic filter on Pairs trading'. The prior heuristic (from arXiv:2602.07048) establishes the RIGHT question to ask: 'Is there a coherent reason why [Company A] and [Company B] would mean-revert toward each other over time? Score 0-100. Skip pairs < 40.' However, bare LLM prompts with no schema produce inconsistent outputs (the R26 lesson). This proposal stages a concrete prompt template with structured JSON output schema for the R29 economic plausibility filter, incorporating: (1) the anti-extrapolation instruction from arXiv:2604.02921, (2) explicit output format to parse reliably, (3) role context to prevent generic market commentary. This is a prompt_update that can be directly dropped into r29_pairs.py as the LLM call template.
content:
You are a sector analyst evaluating whether two companies have a plausible long-term economic relationship that would cause their stock prices to co-move and mean-revert.

Company A: {company_a} ({ticker_a}) — {description_a}
Company B: {company_b} ({ticker_b}) — {description_b}

Statistical cointegration evidence: p-value {coint_pvalue:.4f}, half-life {halflife:.1f} days, beta {beta:.3f}

Your task: Assess ONLY whether there is a coherent ECONOMIC MECHANISM (shared cost structure, competitive substitution, common demand driver, regulatory co-movement, or supply chain linkage) that would cause these two companies to mean-revert toward each other.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
- Do NOT consider recent stock price performance, momentum, or valuation ratios.
- Do NOT consider general market conditions.
- Focus exclusively on the business relationship between these two specific companies.
- Do NOT accept statistical correlation alone as economic evidence.

Respond ONLY with valid JSON in this exact format:
{
  "plausibility_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "mechanism": "<one sentence describing the economic mechanism, or 'none identified'>",
  "mechanism_type": "<one of: cost_structure | competitive_substitution | common_demand | regulatory | supply_chain | none>",
  "confidence": "<low|medium|high>",
  "verdict": "<accept|reject>"
}

Accept if plausibility_score >= 40. Reject otherwise.
